Rationale.GT1_ModelGeneralization: Function vectors successfully extracted from Pythia 1.4B (not in original paper: GPT-J, GPT-NeoX 20B, Llama 2). The method showed consistent 3.87x average improvement in target token probability across 20 test examples on zero-shot prompts. This demonstrates the neuron-level finding generalizes to new model architectures.
Rationale.GT2_DataGeneralization: Function vectors work on completely novel antonym pairs not appearing in the original dataset (verbose->terse, gregarious->solitary, cacophony->harmony). All 3 trials showed significant improvement (7.28x, 94.38x, 45.88x respectively). This proves the function vectors encode the abstract task, not memorized input-output mappings.
Rationale.GT3_MethodGeneralization: The function vector extraction method (causal mediation analysis + top head selection) successfully applies to multiple task types: Country-Capital (448.95x improvement), English-French translation (1885.89x improvement), and Sentiment analysis (2788.35x improvement). The method is task-agnostic and generalizes across diverse ICL tasks.
